question: Which alloys are the intake and exhaust valves made from?
note: intake nickel chromium; exhaust silichrome

question: Why is metallic sodium put inside some exhaust valves?
note: liquefies at operating temperature and splashes between head and stem, carrying heat to the valve guide

question: How hot can an exhaust valve get?
note: in excess of 1300 F (704.4 C)

question: What keeps the intake valve cooler than the exhaust valve?
note: the incoming intake mixture cools it; the exhaust valve is heated by burnt gases passing it

question: Valve timing is measured against what, and in what units?
note: crankshaft position, in degrees

question: Why would you change when the valves open and close?
note: to tailor the engine so it makes peak power in a chosen speed range

question: What stops a diesel running away when it is barely loaded?
note: the governor limits injected fuel; full fuel at part load would overspeed the engine and destroy it

question: What physically drives a diesel governor?
note: centrifugal flyweights, or an air-pressure differential

question: What goes wrong if a silencer restricts the flow too much?
note: back pressure causes loss of power and economy, and overheating

question: Why are exhaust parts coated with aluminium or zinc?
note: to retard corrosion; stainless is used sparingly because of cost

question: How many degrees of crankshaft rotation make up one full four-stroke cycle?
note: 720 degrees - two revolutions, each stroke 180

question: What does the antidiesel solenoid do when you switch the ignition off?
note: it is deenergised so the throttle shuts tight, cutting off the mixture and stopping run-on

question: Why does switching on the air conditioning raise the idle speed?
note: a solenoid boosts idle to compensate for the compressor load and prevent stalling

question: In a P-type semiconductor, which way do the holes appear to travel?
note: toward the negative terminal, while electrons move hole to hole toward the positive

question: Does it matter whether the wire moves or the magnet moves?
note: no - only relative movement matters, so that lines of force are cut

question: What is a battery case made of?
note: hard rubber or polypropylene plastic, resistant to acid and mechanical shock

question: How is a battery marked once its electrolyte has been diluted?
note: a tag giving full-charge specific gravity plus a 1-inch white spot painted on top

question: What parts make up a vibrating current regulator?
note: soft iron core, heavy current coil, spring-held contact points, and a resistance across the points

question: How does the regulator stop the generator exceeding its rated output?
note: it cuts resistance into the circuit as output rises

question: How does the no-charge warning lamp know the alternator has stopped charging?
note: a coil energised by a stator winding closes the points only while output sustains operating voltage; open points mean it is not producing

question: Why does adding a capacitor make the test lamp flash brighter when the points open?
note: it speeds up the collapse of the magnetic field

question: What is blackout lighting for?
note: to let the driver operate in total darkness and to show vehicle position to the vehicle ahead or behind, with illumination restricted

question: Why does the magnetic fuel gauge need no voltage regulator?
note: supply variation affects both coils equally, so the differential between them is unchanged - it is self-regulating

question: What is the magnetic fuel gauge sensitive to?
note: road shock and sudden voltage changes

question: What is the contact angle of a flat thrust bearing?
note: 90 degrees - the load line is parallel with the shaft axis

question: What does a double-row angular-contact bearing give you that a single-row one does not?
note: rigid lengthwise support in both directions rather than only one

question: On a fully floating axle, what loads do the shafts actually carry?
note: turning effort (torque) only; the housing carries the weight and differential stresses

question: What ultimately limits how hard a vehicle can be slowed?
note: the coefficient of friction between tyre and road

question: What actually moves the shoes on an air-braked truck, compared with a hydraulic system?
note: pneumatic uses a rotating cam on a camshaft driven by the air system; hydraulic uses fluid pressure in a cylinder

question: Why do the side rails of truck frames follow standard widths?
note: so stock transmissions, transfer assemblies and rear axles can be mounted

question: Why is the frame of a prime mover built heavier than a normal truck's?
note: extra reinforcement of side rails and rear crossmembers for towing stresses

question: What kind of pump generates the injection pressure in a PSB system?
note: a plunger-type pump driven by a camshaft
